samples.summary: TextEditor.handleIndent/handleOutdent's non-list (marginLeft) branch is restructured but never exercised by any test
samples.evidence: The diff rewrites `handleIndent`/`handleOutdent` in `text-editor.ts` from a single if/else walker into `recordCursorForHistory()` + `doc.batch()` + `applyListLevelChanges()` + a second `forEachBlockInSelection` pass that early-returns on list items and applies `marginLeft` otherwise. The only keyboard tests for these handlers are the new `pressIndentKey` / Cmd+[ cases in `packages/docs/test/view/editor-tab-bullet.test.ts` (lines 107-119, 951), and every one of them uses list items only. Grepping the whole docs package for `'['`/`']'` key dispatch yields only `text-editor.ts:1323/1329` and those two test sites; `editor.indent()`/`api.indent()` callers exercise the *editor.ts* and *text-box-editor.ts* copies of the logic, not this one. So Cmd+] / Cmd+[ on a paragraph (the general indent shortcut) could silently become a no-op — or double-apply for a mixed list+paragraph selection — with the suite fully green.

samples.summary: Four of the new normalizeListLevel sinks (pdf-painter x2, table-renderer, peer-cursor, paint-layout) have no poisoned-level test
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/test/model/list-level.test.ts` states outright that it covers "One representative sink, on purpose" and leaves the PDF painter, the table renderer and the peer cursor to the band's unit test. Grepping `packages/docs/test/export/pdf-painter.test.ts` for `listLevel|1e9|Infinity` returns no matches; `table-renderer.test.ts`, `peer-cursor.test.ts` and `paint-layout.test.ts` contain no out-of-band level cases either. The band unit test only proves `normalizeListLevel` itself, not that each call site actually routes the raw attribute through it — a regression that reverted one of those five lines (e.g. back to `block.listLevel ?? 0` in `pdf-painter.ts:367` or `table-renderer.ts:525`) would leave NaN/1e9 coordinates going into pdf-lib or a NaN Map key, with no test failing.

samples.summary: The MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN loop is never tested with a non-finite row height, despite the comment claiming termination "for any height (`Infinity` included)"
samples.evidence: Every Infinity-flavoured pagination test is neutralised before the loop runs: `computeTableLayout` step 5d (`table-layout.ts:317-321`) replaces any non-finite/non-positive row height with `MIN_ROW_HEIGHT`, so `row-height.test.ts`'s `paginateWith(Infinity)`/`NaN` and `numeric-attrs.test.ts`'s `fontSize: Infinity` / `padding: Infinity` cases reach `paginateLayout` with a 20px row. The only test that pokes the layout directly, `table-row-split.test.ts` 'bounds a row no number of pages can hold', sets `tl.rowHeights[0] = contentHeight * 500` — a finite value. Nothing sets `tl.rowHeights[0] = Infinity` (or NaN) after layout, so the loop's behaviour on the input its own doc-comment advertises is untested; if step 5d were ever relaxed, the hang this change exists to prevent would return undetected.
searchedFor: read new tests in row-height.test.ts, numeric-attrs.test.ts, table-row-split.test.ts from the diff

samples.summary: The one-undo-unit claim is only asserted against a MemDocStore subclass; no YorkieDocStore test covers batched list-level writes
samples.evidence: `editor-tab-bullet.test.ts`'s `TracingStore extends MemDocStore` records `writeDepths`/`cursorFlushDepths`, and the text-box test at `text-box-editor.test.ts:~600` explicitly admits "this assertion holds with the batch removed (verified by removing it)" because MemDocStore takes undo units from `snapshot()`. The store where an unbatched write actually costs a half-moved subtree — `YorkieDocStore`, whose `setBlockType` opens its own `withUpdate` and whose `doc.history` entry-per-change semantics the comments repeatedly cite — gets no new test for indent/outdent batching or for the pre-batch presence flush (#523). The frontend test file only adds numeric-band tests. So the real undo-unit behaviour is asserted only against a simulation of it.

samples.summary: The NaN sub-case of 'a poisoned font size inside a cell neither hangs nor floods pages' is non-discriminating
samples.evidence: With `fontSize: NaN` the derived row height is NaN, and even without any of this change `while (consumed < NaN)` is immediately false and the row emits zero fragments — so `expect(result.pages.length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(202)` passes on the pre-change code too. Only the `Infinity` and `1e9` entries in the same loop discriminate. Harmless because it rides along with real cases, but the NaN entry proves nothing about the bound (what it would prove — that the table still renders — is asserted separately in `row-height.test.ts`).

finding.summary: The frontend YorkieDocStore read boundary — the live collaborative path this change exists for — gets no test for any of the new bands
finding.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts` gains its own copies of the guards (`normalizeFontSize` at the inline parse, `isPaintableImageSize`, `normalizeCellPadding` in `parseCellStyle`, `normalizeRowHeight` on the `rowHeights` attribute, `normalizeListLevel` on `listLevel`). This is a *duplicate* parser from `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts`, and only the docs-package copy is covered (`packages/docs/test/model/numeric-attrs.test.ts` and `row-height.test.ts`/`list-level.test.ts` all call `treeNodeToBlock` from `../../src/model/crdt-tree.js`). Grepping `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` for `listLevel|rowHeights|fontSize|padding|image.width|normalize` finds only happy-path values (fontSize 14/18/20, listLevel 0/1) — no `Infinity`, `NaN`, `1e9` or negative case anywhere in `packages/frontend/tests` for these attributes. So if a band is wired to the wrong field, dropped, or inverted in the frontend copy, nothing fails: frontend also has no `tsc` lane, and the two parsers can silently drift. The frontend copy is the one that actually reads a hostile peer's attributes in production.

verdict.reason: The named test file does contain band coverage for all five attributes at the frontend YorkieDocStore read boundary. packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:3388-3499 is a describe block 'bands the numeric attributes a peer can write' that reads back through a SECOND store over the same Yorkie document (peerRead, line 3389) so the frontend parse path actually executes rather than returning the writer's cache. It asserts hostile values for each band: fontSize (3416-3421: Infinity/NaN/0/-11 -> undefined, 1e9 -> MAX_FONT_SIZE), image size (3434-3437: Infinity/NaN/1e9/negative -> dropped), cell padding (3449-3453: Infinity/NaN/-4 -> undefined, 1e9 -> MAX_CELL_PADDING), rowHeights (3467-3474, including a positional test that a dropped entry does not shift neighbours), and listLevel (3494-3497: Infinity/NaN/-4 -> 0, 1e9 -> MAX_LIST_LEVEL). The store under test is the real one over a real yorkie.Document with no mocks (lines 1-4, 26-37), so the tests fail if a band is dropped, inverted, or wired to the wrong field. Additionally, the frontend does not hold its own copies of the guards: yorkie-doc-store.ts:50-55 imports normalizeListLevel/normalizeRowHeight/normalizeFontSize/normalizeCellPadding/isPaintableImageSize from '@wafflebase/docs', so the guard bodies are shared, and only the wiring is frontend-local — which is precisely what this describe block exercises. The finding's grep result ('only happy-path values, no Infinity/NaN/1e9 or negative anywhere in packages/frontend/tests') is directly contradicted by these lines in the working tree.
